clue.text: Gently hit spinner of the highest quality

parts.note: to tip a ball is to strike it lightly
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praising a batsman who delicately dabs a slow bowler's delivery away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket, but here it is the child's toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal adjective for something excellent, first-rate or in perfect condition.

clue.text: Unfairness within players' organization

parts.note: a direct synonym
Equity is the British trade union for actors

explanation.surface: Injustice going on inside a sports club or players' association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests sport, but they are actors, and Equity is the UK actors' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequity means a lack of justice or fairness, the opposite of equity in its moral sense.

clue.text: Boston incident Alice joined in

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1773 colonial protest in which British tea was dumped into the harbour
second meaning: the Mad Hatter's gathering in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A woman called Alice took part in some Boston event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boston protest and the March Hare's table in Lewis Carroll's story share this name for a social gathering.

clue.text: Professional team-mate is very close

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports pro and a fellow squad member are close friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team-mate' looks like one word, but splits into team (XI, eleven in Roman numerals) and mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Proximate means nearest or immediately adjacent, from Latin proximus, closest.

clue.text: On a subject giving those people a twitch

parts.note: the plural pronoun for a group pointed out
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary muscle twitch

explanation.surface: Discussing some topic makes certain listeners fidget nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thematic relates to a theme, meaning it concerns a particular topic or recurring idea.

clue.text: Trinity crew?

parts.note: a trinity is a group of three
a rowing crew is the people manning a vessel

explanation.surface: The rowing team of Trinity College, Cambridge or Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic novel about three friends on a Thames boating holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's three heroes afloat on the river are literally a trio forming a small boat's company.

clue.text: Fringe material for group of stars in club

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
the Ram is the constellation Aries

explanation.surface: Costume trimmings for a band of celebrities at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars in club' suggests celebrities in a nightclub; the stars are a constellation and the club a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is knotted cord or thread work, traditionally used to make decorative fringes and trimmings.

clue.text: Very careful, albeit poetically imprecise

parts.note: tho' is the clipped form of though used in verse
a rough estimate is an imprecise one

explanation.surface: Describing someone as meticulous, though perhaps a little loose with words.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough person is painstaking and leaves nothing undone, attending to every detail.

clue.text: Course in old monarch's rule

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a direct synonym

explanation.surface: A course of study in how an ancient king governed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks academic, but it is part of a meal, and 'old monarch' is Old King Cole.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage, served as a side dish or course in a meal.

clue.text: Attack to support left?

parts.note: read cryptically, to support a party is to be one of its members
Labour is the main left-wing party in British politics

explanation.surface: A call to go on the offensive in defence of the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: to back the left is to 'be Labour', Labour being Britain's main left-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone is to assail them, whether with blows or with repeated criticism.

clue.text: Artist's following train

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the group of painters influenced by a master
second meaning: to teach or discipline someone

explanation.surface: A painter's entourage boarding a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun, but it is the verb meaning to educate.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of painting is a body of followers of one style, and to school a person is to educate them.

clue.text: Churchman seen about four, giving patient help

indicators.note: something seen wrapped about another thing surrounds it on both sides

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest
four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clergyman visiting the sick at about four o'clock to offer comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient help' sounds like forbearance, but the patient is someone being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A curative remedy is one that heals, so it provides aid to people under medical care.

clue.text: Dialect to set in Paris? Not right

indicators.note: something set in another is placed inside it
not having right means the letter standing for right is dropped

parts.note: the French capital taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some regional speech is wrong for a story located in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in Paris' reads as a story's location, but 'set in' tells you to insert the first word into the city's name once R has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Patois is a regional form of speech, often a non-standard local variety of a language such as French.

clue.text: Oppose return of painting and poetry

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for painting is read from its end

parts.note: painting is one form of art
verse is metrical writing

explanation.surface: Objecting to a comeback for traditional painting and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to traverse is to deny or contradict an allegation, so it can mean to counter or resist.

clue.text: Pithy expression for a limited period

parts.note: brief and to the point
a term is a word or phrase

explanation.surface: A concise phrase that applies only temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-term describes something lasting or planned for only a brief time ahead, not permanently.

clue.text: Dramatist's repeated literary extremes

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters at each end

parts.note: the first and last letters of literary
the same pair of letters written a second time

explanation.surface: A playwright's habit of going to literary extremes again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: John Lyly was an Elizabethan dramatist and author of Euphues. The definition 'Dramatist's' is completed by an implied 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lyly wrote plays for court performance in the age of Elizabeth I, before Shakespeare's prime.

clue.text: One unlikely to win from such a distance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an outsider in a race or contest
second meaning: a picture taken or an attempt made from far away

explanation.surface: A competitor shooting at a far-off target has little chance of success.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider at big odds is so called, and a film shot or a strike taken from far off bears the same name.

clue.text: Bound with decorative fastening in game

parts.note: a bound is a jump
a frog is an ornamental braided loop and toggle on a coat

explanation.surface: Tied up with an ornamental clasp during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'tied', but it means a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game in which players vault over others who are crouching down.

clue.text: Lawrence as playwright

definitions.meaning: first meaning: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under an assumed surname
second meaning: George Bernard, the Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: D. H. or T. E. Lawrence considered as a writer for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence, 'of Arabia', changed his name by deed poll in 1927, and the dramatist was a friend of his.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence of Arabia took the alias T. E. Shaw, and George Bernard Shaw wrote Pygmalion and Saint Joan.

clue.text: Pay for Irishman and refuse change

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it
Pat is a stock name for an Irishman

explanation.surface: Buying a round for an Irish friend and declining your coins back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse change' suggests turning down coins, but it means rejecting alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand pat comes from poker, where a player keeps the hand dealt, so it means sticking firmly to a position.

clue.text: Salt at sea in Near East

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disoriented, so these letters are in disorder

parts.note: the fodder taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Salt obtained from the ocean in the Levant region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt at sea' looks like sea salt; 'at sea' is the signal and 'Near East' the eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenate is a chemical salt of arsenic acid, used for example in pesticides.

clue.text: Place to land for her pilot, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given could be arranged another way

parts.note: the fodder taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A landing site laid on for a female aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliport is an airport for helicopters, a site where such aircraft touch down and take off.

clue.text: Trainer of boxer after title, right?

parts.note: a handle is a name or title
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fighter's coach came along once the championship was won.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer looks like a prizefighter but is the dog breed; a handler trains and controls dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A handler is a person who trains and controls an animal such as a police or show dog.

clue.text: Open wide — key needs copying

parts.note: G is a musical key
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: A locksmith reports that a door is unlocked, but the key has to be duplicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' points at locks, but here it is one of the musical keys A to G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping describes something with a broad opening, like a mouth or wound stretched apart.

clue.text: One present that's easily damaged at first

parts.note: the word at, placed at the start
tender means delicate or sore

explanation.surface: A fragile gift that suffered harm right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' suggests a gift, but here it means being there; 'at first' tells you to put AT in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An attender is someone who attends, so a person who is there at a meeting or event.

clue.text: Career for Luther after Reformation

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so these letters are reformed into a new order

parts.note: the fodder taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: Martin Luther's professional life following the Protestant upheaval he started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is not a job but the verb meaning to rush along out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: To career and to hurtle both mean to move at great speed in a headlong, uncontrolled way.

clue.text: Give too much money, about pound, for ham

indicators.note: about here means going round the outside of the next item

parts.note: to pay more than is due
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign

explanation.surface: Paying well over the odds at the butcher's for a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the meat, but it is a verb: to act badly and showily.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to act in an exaggerated manner, and to overplay a role is exactly that.

clue.text: One or two felines

definitions.note: one feline, the clue's last word carried over

wordplay.note: a big striped wild cat followed by the ordinary household pet

explanation.surface: A vague count of a few cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of a single animal spells out two cat names one after the other, hence 'one or two'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger cat is a small striped wild cat of South America, also called the oncilla.

clue.text: French import trade

parts.note: surface reading: commerce in goods brought in from France
setter's reading: a word borrowed from French, meaning trade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Import trade' reads as one commercial phrase, but the clue splits as a loanword from France plus its meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A métier is a person's occupation or line of work, and in English also their forte.
